key_insight: GINNGER learns thermodynamic generators rather than constitutive operators, yielding rheological models that satisfy the first and second laws of thermodynamics by construction.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports transferable, physically consistent constitutive modeling of complex fluids across deformation protocols and flow geometries.
method: Embed the GENERIC formalism to constrain learned thermodynamic generators.
Represent microstructural states in the polymer conformation tensor’s intrinsic eigenspace.
Combine shear, extensional, and mixed-flow data to discover a single constitutive model.
evidence_signal: Validation uses high-fidelity simulations to reconstruct constitutive behavior and predict complex flow fields in previously unseen geometries; the abstract provides no quantitative error metrics.
watch_item: Transfer to experimental materials remains to be established, particularly when microstructural state data are sparse or noisy.
paper_title: A GENERIC-Informed Neural Network for Generative Rheology
